heading: INT. COUNTY FAIR - PIE TENT - DAY

units.text: INT. COUNTY FAIR - PIE TENT - DAY
A canvas tent in the August glare.
Long tables of judged pies, blue ribbons pinned like medals.
Flies drone.
A fan turns slowly overhead.
PENELOPE "PENNY" ASHWORTH-BELL, 16, in a gingham apron two sizes too large, stands guard over a single lattice-topped peach pie.
Her fingers are stained with flour and nerves.
Her grandmother, MAUDE ASHWORTH-BELL, 70s, enormous sunhat, sits on a folding chair behind her and says nothing, in the way only grandmothers can.
Down the row, JUDGE THEODORE "TEDDY" CROMWELL, 60s, seersucker suit, moves from pie to pie with a silver fork and a stern expression.
A late arrival bursts in, breathless.
WILLIAM "WILLIE" TANAKA, 17, in a rumpled work shirt, grease on his cheek, carrying a pie plate wrapped in a dish towel.
Penny! Penny, I made it.
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: Willie. The deadline was ten.
units.name: PENNY

units.text: It's ten-oh-four.
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: That's closed.
units.name: PENNY

units.text: They can't close on a four-minute margin.
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: They can. They have.
units.name: PENNY

units.text: Maude lifts her chin a fraction beneath the hat.
Four minutes is four minutes, young man.
units.name: MAUDE

units.text: Mrs. Ashworth-Bell. I didn't see you there.
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: Few people do. It's a gift.
units.name: MAUDE

units.text: I stayed up all night. I burned the first one. And the second.
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: I can smell it.
units.name: PENNY

units.text: It's the sacrifice.
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: She cannot help it.
She laughs.
Quickly claps a hand over her mouth.
Judge Cromwell reaches the end of the row and looks up, eyebrow arched.
Is there a disturbance?
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: No, sir.
units.name: PENNY

units.text: Yes, sir. I'm late.
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: Hm.
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: He studies the dish towel in Willie's hands.
The corner has stained with something dark and sticky.
What have you there, son?
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: A blackberry, sir. Mostly.
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: Mostly.
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: There was an incident with the oven.
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: I'll bet.
units.name: MAUDE

units.text: Cromwell holds out his hand.
Willie hesitates, then unwraps the towel.
The pie inside is lopsided, the crust charred at one edge, the filling bubbling over like lava.
Penny stares at it.
Then at Willie.
Then at the judge.
Sir, he's late. By the rules, he can't--
units.name: PENNY

units.text: Miss Ashworth-Bell. I have judged this tent for thirty-one years. I have never once seen a pie arrive so wretchedly.
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: Thank you, sir?
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: It was not a compliment.
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: He cuts a sliver with the silver fork.
Lifts it.
Tastes.
Everyone holds still.
The fan turns.
A fly lands on the nearest table and thinks better of it.
Burnt sugar. Lemon zest. A touch of black pepper.
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: My mother's trick.
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: Hm.
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: He takes another bite.
Then a third.
Then, with a visible effort at composure, sets down the fork.
The rules are the rules. Your entry is disqualified.
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: Yes, sir.
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: I'm sorry, Willie.
units.name: PENNY

units.text: However.
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: He turns and walks to the head table.
Takes a small rosette from a tray.
Not blue.
Green.
Pins it to the lapel of Willie's work shirt with brisk, painless precision.
That is the Judge's Indulgence. It is awarded perhaps once a decade.
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: Penny, I think I'm going to cry.
units.name: WILLIE

units.text: Don't. You'll get it in the pie.
units.name: PENNY

units.text: Miss Ashworth-Bell, your peach has a fine lattice. Competent. Tidy.
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: Tidy?
units.name: PENNY

units.text: First place.
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: Penny's mouth falls open.
Maude, behind her, finally smiles beneath the hat.
You beat me by being late!
units.name: PENNY
paren: to Willie, at once with Cromwell

units.text: The tent is closed to further questions.
units.name: CROMWELL

units.text: He marches off with the silver fork.
The two teenagers look at each other, unable to speak.
Well. That's two ribbons and a fire hazard. Come, children. Cake.
units.name: MAUDE

units.text: She sweeps out.
Penny and Willie follow, still grinning, still stunned, the green rosette bobbing on his chest.
